title: Tab-completing the :tag command results in a crash if a tagname is too long
body:

    ```
    Run :checkhealth for more info
    ```
    </details>
- `vim -u DEFAULTS` (version: 8.2.2536) behaves differently? Yes
- Operating system/version: Solus 4.2 Fortitude
- Terminal name/version: Konsole 20.12.2
- `$TERM`: xterm-256color

### Steps to reproduce using `nvim -u NORC`

Create a `tags` file with this in it:

```
aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa	file	/^pattern$/;"	f
```

Launch Neovim and tab-complete the `:tag` command:

```
nvim -u NORC +'call feedkeys(":tag \<Tab>", "t")'
```

### Actual behaviour

Neovim crashes:

```
*** stack smashing detected ***: terminated
```

### Expected behaviour

No crash

It looks like the crash is caused by the length of the tagname being over 102 characters long. If I delete one "a" from the tagname, Neovim doesn't crash.

I ran into this bug when I generated tags for the Neovim codebase (with `exhuberant ctags`, not `universal ctags`)

I have tested this with the Neovim 0.4.4 appimage and the bug is not present (I can't build Neovim past a certain commit so I was unable to bisect)
